speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I'm Dr. Agent. Can you describe the skin lesions and tell me how long you've had the wrist pain and fever?

speaker: Patient
text: 17-year-old male. The patient presents with a 3-day history of pain in his left wrist, which worsened this morning accompanied by chills and malaise. He recounts having a self-resolving left knee pain the previous week. Reports recent return from a camping trip in Minnesota. Sexually active with one female partner. No history of trauma to the wrist.

speaker: Doctor
text: Given your recent camping trip in Minnesota and the pattern of migratory joint pain, I need to know if you noticed any tick bites or a circular, expanding rash on your skin. Have you experienced any neurological symptoms like facial drooping or numbness?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Pain in the left wrist. I also have Chills, Malaise, Painless violaceous vesiculopustular lesions on both wrists and hands, Swelling and erythema of the left wrist, Severe tenderness to palpation and passive movement of the left wrist.

speaker: Doctor
text: The presence of painless violaceous vesiculopustular lesions on the hands and wrists, combined with fever and monoarticular arthritis, is highly suggestive of meningococcemia. REQUEST TEST: Blood culture.

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Pending at the time of examination

speaker: Doctor
text: Do you have a headache, neck stiffness, or sensitivity to light, which might indicate meningitis? Also, have you noticed any bruising or petechiae elsewhere on your body?

speaker: Patient
text: Past medical history: Otherwise healthy with no significant past medical history. Social history: Admits to being sexually active with one female partner who uses a diaphragm for contraception. Recently went on a camping trip to Minnesota.

speaker: Doctor
text: The violaceous lesions and monoarticular arthritis are classic for meningococcemia, but I must rule out disseminated gonococcal infection given his sexual history. REQUEST TEST: Gram stain and culture of wrist aspirate.

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: WBC >50,000 /μL (markedly elevated); Gram Stain: Gram-negative diplococci seen

speaker: Doctor
text: The presence of Gram-negative diplococci in the joint aspirate confirms Disseminated Gonococcal Infection. DIAGNOSIS READY: Disseminated Gonococcal Infection
